verdict.reason:
PASS — the debate does not clear the bar for a long-term wealth mandate at this entry.
• Compliance is clean: long-only shares, no blocklist, 0/4 trades today, 0.0 pt of the 30 pt drawdown cap used, 0% sector concentration — nothing blocks a buy, so this is a judgment call, not a floor call.
• The desk, Research Manager, and both Bear and Conservative risk officers converge on the same fact: FCF -$3,269M TTM against $13,920M capex and $74,103M net debt makes this a bond-proxy, not a wealth compounder — the mandate's stated emphasis on free-cash-flow consistency weighs against, not for.
• The Aggressive's asymmetry case (+19.7% to the $99.24 consensus target vs -1.0% to the $82.09 low) is real, but the target is a Street mean with a hold rating (2.6) and EPS estimates cut 1.5% over 90 days — it requires multiple expansion on 0% TTM revenue growth.
• The Google PPA is the one structural bull datum and it carries no contract size, term, or rate-base figure anywhere on the sheet — paying for it now is paying for narrative.
• Entry quality is poor for a fresh position: -14.0% over 64 days, 10.1% below the 200-day average, -4.4% under the 20-day SMA at $86.65 — RSI 20 argues against selling, not for initiating.
• The Balanced 2.0% compromise is the strongest counter, but with Q4 earnings 40 days out (2026-11-05) as the first hard test of the data-center thesis, the cost of waiting is small against the cost of being early on an unquantified catalyst.
verdict.kill_criterion: Flip to a buyer on either a daily close back above the 20-day SMA at $86.65, or Q4 results on 2026-11-05 showing the Google PPA converting to disclosed rate-base growth with TTM revenue growth above the current 0%.
